stops.note: 'woman who spins', with the feminine agent ending -ster, as in Webster (woman weaver) and Baxter (woman baker)
John Minsheu's dictionary of 1617 calls it a term 'added in Obligations, Evidences, and Writings, unto maids unmarried'; by 1719 it meant an older unmarried woman

current_meaning: an unmarried woman, typically an older one (now often considered offensive)
